assessment.summary: A present, quantified concentration risk — a single country supplies the U.S. with a major share of over a third of the minerals it most depends on importing — that has already produced real 2025 supply shocks and price spikes, with escalation to a broader multi-country industrial disruption a live risk.
assessment.timeframe: Ongoing and worsening; the U.S. critical minerals list and import-reliance figures are reassessed annually, and 2025 already saw China's export controls disrupt automaker production and double the value of U.S. processed-mineral imports.

claims.text: The U.S. remained reliant on imports from China as a major source for 14 of the 33 critical minerals for which the United States most depends on imports (USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026).

Net imports of processed metals and materials more than doubled by value, from $77 billion in 2024 to $185 billion in 2025, and the Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026 covers 14 minerals, from antimony to tungsten, that China restricts exporting to the United States (USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026).

The Department of the Interior's final 2025 List of Critical Minerals, published November 6, 2025 by USGS, identifies 60 minerals vital to the U.S. economy and national security whose supply chains face potential disruption risk, adding 10 new minerals — including copper, silver, and uranium — to the list.

description: The energy, defense, and technology sectors depend on a small set of minerals — rare earths, lithium, cobalt, antimony, and dozens of others — whose mining and, especially, refining are geographically concentrated in a handful of countries. Export restrictions, geopolitical tension, or a shock to a single dominant supplier can disrupt processed-material flows worldwide with little substitution available in the short term, as China's 2025 export controls on rare earths and antimony already demonstrated by forcing automakers to cut production and sending prices sharply higher.
name: Critical Mineral Supply Chain Disruption
